title: Parent (top-level) group positions / office bearers
status: SHIPPED backend on the Convex deployment. Native builds its own UI against the functions below. Election + admin controls already existed for parent groups; this adds ONLY the position/role designation (SPEC 5).
concept: Assign role titles (President, Chairman, Secretary, Treasurer, etc.) to members of a TOP-LEVEL group (a normal group, i.e. a 'group' conversation with NO parentConversationId). This mirrors the existing sub-group positions feature but for regular groups. There is NO 'show in mother' concept here (parent groups have no mother).
storage: Rows live in the same underlying table as sub-group positions, keyed by the group's conversationId. Do not read the table directly; use the functions below.

roles.assignOrClear: Any group admin (chief admin, creator, or admin) may assign/update/clear a position.
roles.reorder: Only the Chief Admin (or creator) may reorder positions.

args.userId: Id<users> (member to assign; must be a participant of the group)
args.title: string. Non-empty to set/update (max 60 chars). Empty/whitespace CLEARS the position.

setPosition.returns: { cleared: boolean } — cleared:true when the title was empty and any existing position was removed; cleared:false when a position was set/updated.
errors: NOT_FOUND — group not found / not a group
BAD_REQUEST — conversation is a sub group (use subGroups.setPosition instead), or user is not a member of the group
FORBIDDEN — caller is not a group admin

listPositions.returns: Array<{ userId: Id<users>, title: string, order: number | null }> sorted by manual order (lower first), then title, then creation time. Returns [] if the caller is not a member or the conversation is not a top-level group.
listPositions.notes: Reactive. Use this to render role labels against member names in the group.

args.orderedUserIds: Array<Id<users>> — full desired top-to-bottom order of members who hold positions. Members without a position are ignored. Any positioned members omitted keep their relative order but sort below the listed ones.

setPositionOrder.returns: { ordered: number } — count of position rows that were assigned an order.
errors: FORBIDDEN — caller is not the chief admin/creator

relationshipToSubGroups: For SUB groups, keep using api.subGroups.setPosition / listPositions / setPositionVisibility / setPositionOrder (those still have the showInMother option). For TOP-LEVEL groups, use api.groupPositions.* documented here. Calling a subGroups position function on a top-level group throws, and vice versa.
